calls.head: The Predators’ edge in depth
calls.body: The Predators are around the middle of the league for depth, and the Maple Leafs are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Nashville found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Nashville usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots. Not tonight: an 8.5% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.8% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: O'Reilly reaches 900 points, but the Predators lose
paras: Never count the Maple Leafs out. Steven Stamkos struck first for the Predators on the power play early in the first. Nils Höglander made it 2-0 just under two minutes later, with Filip Forsberg picking up his 400th NHL assist on the goal. The second period brought five goals. Höglander scored again early in the period to make it 3-0. John Tavares and William Nylander scored just over two minutes apart later in the period to cut Nashville’s lead to 3-2. Stamkos scored his second of the night midway through the second to make it 4-2 for the Predators, with Ryan O'Reilly picking up his 900th NHL point on the goal. Gavin McKenna, in his fourth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Auston Matthews, just over a minute later to pull the Maple Leafs within one. Jack Roslovic scored his first goal for Toronto midway through the third to tie it 4-4. Toronto had a goal taken off for offside later in the period, though it didn’t end up costing them. Matthews won it in overtime. Matthews finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Nylander had a goal and two assists.

The Predators were outshot 37-25, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Anthony Stolarz made 21 saves for the Maple Leafs, and Juuse Saros stopped 32 of 37 at the other end. The Maple Leafs improved to 2-2-0 and climbed to fifth in the Atlantic, while the Preds dropped to 1-1-1 but climbed to fifth in the Central.

items.text: Steven Stamkos passed Jarome Iginla and Joe Sakic for 17th on the NHL’s all-time goals list, with 627.
Auston Matthews moved into a tie for ninth in overtime goals since the NHL went to 3-on-3 overtime in 2015-16, with 15.
Auston Matthews scored again against Nashville, and has seven goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Jayden Struble faces his old team, Montréal, on Thursday.
